stories.title: Police hunt suspect after deadly Berlin Pride car attack
stories.summary: German police are searching for a 21-year-old suspect believed linked to Islamist circles after a car ploughed into a crowd near Berlin's Gay Pride celebrations, killing one person and wounding 16 others. The incident shattered what had been a day of celebration for hundreds of thousands attending Christopher Street Day, one of Europe's largest Pride events, and left revellers fleeing a central Berlin park as sirens echoed through the night. Police said the suspect's vehicle was later found abandoned a few hundred metres from the heart of the festivities in Tiergarten park. A manhunt involving helicopters and officers from several German states is under way across the capital.

stories.title: Iran war spreads to Red Sea and Caspian as Gulf quiet
stories.summary: The Iran war broadened over the weekend despite a pause in US strikes. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast and Iran accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea. The US military said yesterday its naval blockade against Iran "remains in full effect" but did not explain why it halted a streak of 13 nights of escalating strikes. There were also no weekend reports of attacks by Iran on neighbours, similar to its daily rejoinders to the US attacks.

stories.title: Man arrested over alleged historic sexual abuse at FAI
stories.summary: Gardaí investigating allegations of historical sexual abuse at the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) three decades ago have arrested former coach Eamonn Collins. He was arrested in Dublin yesterday morning by officers from the Garda National Protective Services Bureau. The allegations were also detailed in the Sunday Independent newspaper. In a written statement issued by his solicitors in 2024, Mr Collins said he "emphatically and unreservedly denies any improper relationship or conduct by him while he was involved as a coach on a football training course in west county Dublin that commenced in 1996, which is more than 25 years ago".

stories.title: Wildfires force huge exodus in France and Spain
stories.summary: Thousands crowded into emergency shelters in France and Spain after wildfires drove more than 300,000 people from their homes and holiday accommodation. The blazes have destroyed houses, displaced people on a massive scale and triggered one of the largest peacetime civilian evacuation operations ever carried out in France, with major fires still burning in both countries. One person was killed in eastern Spain and fresh evacuations were ordered around the French city of Bordeaux and the Spanish capital Madrid as authorities warned of another difficult night. Families slept on camp beds in exhibition halls and gymnasiums after fleeing walls of smoke and flames that swept through forests and tourist areas, leaving residents and holidaymakers uncertain if they would be able to return.

stories.title: Burnham's flurry of new plans met with intense scrutiny
stories.summary: As a seasoned politician, new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be all too aware of the old adage about a week being a long time in politics. This week is undoubtedly the most consequential he has faced in his decades in public life. As he was driven through the gates of Downing Street on Monday to make that all too familiar walk to the legendary black door of Number 10, he had reached a post he has long coveted, but which will bring scrutiny on a scale he has never seen. An early indicator of just how much his every word will now be parsed came when he was asked about how the income tax threshold had been a major topic on the doorsteps when he was campaigning for the parliamentary seat in Makerfield that paved his way into Downing Street.

stories.title: Pilots become first mother and daughter to fly together
stories.summary: Two Aer Lingus pilots made history earlier this week after becoming the first mother and daughter to operate a commercial flight together for the airline. Captain Sonya Bissett, who has been a commercial pilot with Aer Lingus for over 27 years, was joined on flight EI 650 from Dublin to Frankfurt by her daughter, First Officer Lara Danaher. While there have been many previous examples of family members working together on an Aer Lingus flight, it is the first time a mother and daughter operated a flight together in a proud moment for both Ms Bissett and Ms Danaher. "I remember when Lara was about four years of age, she always knew two pilots 'flew the plane'. When I was putting on my uniform for work one day she said, 'I know what mum, when I grow up, I’ll be a pilot, that way I can come to work with you and we can fly the plane together'," she said.

stories.title: Preview: Mayo must be perfect but Kerry have more leeway
stories.summary: A dramatic, story-laden 2026 football championship reaches its conclusion with the meeting of Mayo and Kerry and murmurings of a season with a standing amongst the greatest. Semi-final weekend did sully that suggestion somewhat as Louth were outclassed and Dublin were, well, outraged, but a big final - crowned with a Mayo win - would elevate it right up there. In the championship to date, seven games have required extra-time. Some 15 matches have been won by three points or less. The lowest score by a winning team was the 0-15 Tipperary managed against Waterford in Munster. Pre FRC enhancements, 15 points would have won many a game. In fact, in 2024, the last season of the old rules, 0-15 would have been enough to win an inconceivable 37 championship matches. This year, it would have won just eight.

stories.title: Road safety theme for Reek Sunday on Croagh Patrick
stories.summary: Thousands of pilgrims from Ireland and abroad are expected to climb Croagh Patrick in Co Mayo today for the annual Reek Sunday pilgrimage. Masses will be celebrated hourly in a small church on the summit of Croagh Patrick from 8am until 2pm and confessions will also take place on the summit. In a homily in Saint Mary's Church, Westport last night, Archbishop of Tuam and Bishop of Killala Francis Duffy said road safety was the theme chosen for this Reek Sunday. Archbishop Duffy said behind every statistic lies "trauma, heartache and sadness", adding lives and families can be changed in a single moment.
